key_insight: Large language models struggle to maintain the right belief state over long interactions, and explicit belief-aware training can substantially reduce errors in when to update, preserve, or ignore information.
engineering_relevance: For deployed AI systems, this suggests that robust long-horizon assistants may need structured state management and reward signals tied to belief consistency, not just better prompting.
method: Defines Contextual Belief Management (CBM) as maintaining evidence-aligned beliefs while filtering irrelevant noise.
Introduces BeliefTrack, a closed-world benchmark with finite belief states and symbolic verifiers for exact turn-level scoring.
Tests vanilla LLMs, belief-tracking prompts, reinforcement learning with belief-state rewards, and representation-level steering.
evidence_signal: BeliefTrack covers Rule Discovery and Circuit Diagnosis, enabling exact turn-level evaluation and revealing that RL with belief-state rewards cuts failure rates by 70.9% on average.
watch_item: Results come from closed-world tasks with symbolic verification, so gains may not transfer directly to open-ended real-world dialogue or discovery settings.
paper_title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models
